# laparoskopi

Laparoskopi (laparoscopy) is a minimally invasive surgical procedure that serves as a key focus of quality analysis within the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB) in [[danmark|Danmark]]. Specifically, it constitutes the second subpopulation for national quality indicator 8, where the administration and use of [[epidural|epidural]] anesthesia are closely evaluated [^src1]. In the context of acute surgery, laparoskopi is frequently contrasted with open surgery, known as [[laparotomi|laparotomi]], to assess surgical approaches and anesthetic practices across different hospitals and regions [^src2].

Recent data from the AKDB highlights the prevalence and anesthetic management of laparoskopi in acute surgical settings. In the reporting period from September 1, 2024, to August 31, 2025, the proportion of patients who received an epidural during laparoskopi in Danmark was 39.9% (95% CI: 37.6–42.2) [^src1]. 

Furthermore, longitudinal statistics illustrate a shifting balance between laparoskopi and laparotomi in acute surgical interventions over a three-year span. During the 2024–2025 period, out of 3,250 acute surgical procedures performed in Danmark, 1,814 (55.82%) were laparoskopi, while 1,436 (44.18%) were laparotomi [^src2]. This represents an increase in the proportion of laparoscopic procedures compared to the previous year; in the 2023–2024 period, out of 3,247 acute procedures, 1,667 (51.34%) were laparoskopi and 1,580 (48.66%) were laparotomi [^src2]. Looking back further to the 2022–2023 period, out of 3,214 acute procedures, 1,522 (47.36%) were laparoskopi and 1,692 (52.64%) were laparotomi [^src2]. This data underscores a steady national trend toward minimally invasive techniques, while also revealing significant inter-hospital variation in the implementation of evidence-based anesthesia guidelines.
